general.note: About 60 g. Check the packet, some brands are twice as strong.

tools.name: Pan
tools.note: For the seafood, which is cooked apart from the curry.

tools.name: Colander
tools.note: For thawing and draining the seafood.

steps.title: Thaw the seafood
points: Put the seafood in a colander and run cold water over it until the ice is gone, about 3 minutes.
Leave it to drain, then pat it dry and salt it lightly.
Water left on the seafood is the main reason seafood curry comes out thin.

steps.title: Cut the vegetables
points: Slice the onion thin.
Peel the carrot and cut it into rough chunks, peel the potato and cut it into sixths.
Cut the potato last and leave it in water until it goes in.

steps.title: Brown the onion
points: Cook the onion in the oil over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Take it to a proper golden brown, not just soft.
Add the garlic and ginger for the last minute. This step is where the sweetness comes from.

steps.title: Add the roots
points: Add the carrot and potato and turn them in the onion for 2 minutes.
Coating them in fat first keeps them whole through the simmer.

steps.title: Simmer
points: Pour in the water and add the bay leaf.
Bring it to a boil, skim the foam off, then set the lid ajar and simmer for 15 minutes.
The carrot is ready when a knife goes in without pushing.

steps.title: Melt the roux
points: Turn the heat off and wait a minute for the bubbling to stop.
Break the roux in and stir until it has dissolved completely.
Roux dropped into boiling liquid seizes into lumps.

steps.title: Sear the seafood
points: Melt the butter in the frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the seafood for 1 minute, just until the prawns turn and the squid goes opaque.
Tip the whole lot, butter included, into the pot.

steps.title: Thicken
points: Put the pot back over low heat and stir for 5 minutes.
Keep it below a boil. Hard boiling toughens the seafood and splits the roux.
Taste, then round it out with the milk, honey or soy sauce if it needs it.

steps.title: Serve
points: Spoon the rice onto one side of each plate and ladle the curry beside it.
Fish the bay leaf out as you go.
Leftovers keep a day in the fridge. Warm them below a boil, or the seafood toughens.

troubleshooting.solution: Water came off the seafood, or the pot never came back to heat after the roux. Thaw and dry the seafood properly, and give it the full 5 minutes on low at the end.
Too little water for the roux, or too long at a simmer with the lid off. Loosen it with hot water a splash at a time. It thickens again as it cools.
It went into boiling liquid. Turn the heat off, wait for the bubbles to stop, and break the blocks up small. Lumps that have already formed can be crushed against the side of the pot with the ladle.
It cooked too long. Seafood belongs in the pot for the last few minutes only, and the curry must not boil after it goes in.
The onion was not browned enough. Ten minutes is the floor. For a curry already made, a teaspoon of soy sauce and a teaspoon of honey will fill it out.
Two tablespoons of milk, off the heat, softens it. So does a knob of butter. Neither should be boiled afterwards.
Add the dried seafood straight to the pot after the roux has melted and cook it for 2 minutes over low heat. You lose the browning and keep the texture.
